text: ...I'm falling.
What a strange experience. I stretch out all four limbs like a thin maple leaf, at the mercy of even the slightest gust of wind.

The wind cannot support me, however, and only offers the illusion of briefly soaring in the sky. My body is in the tyrannical grip of gravity, and no matter how comically I struggle, the inevitable result is down, down like someone drowning beneath the waves...
Before today, I'd imagined this to be like those drop tower rides, or bungee jumping. Ah, how foolish I was! I couldn't have been more wrong.
There are so many differences. Take right now, for example: After the initial shock of weightlessness, the gasping wind offers a novel, almost existential experience, a constant barrage of stimuli.
...Correction. I forgot that I'm wearing earmuffs. Judging by how my exposed skin feels, that rather benign 'gasping' of the wind is merely an illusion. It's actually roaring by my ears.
Right now, the only thing that can break through the shrieking gale and reach my ears, is the booming voice of the man behind me.
Well, to be quite honest I'm not exactly okay, but just hearing your voice is a little reassuring.

Right now, Joseph and I are thousands of feet up in the air. As there was no suitable place to land a plane at the site of our expedition, Joseph suggested the exhilarating alternative of a tandem skydive.
Really...? Maybe I should open my eyes and take a look?
No! I'm not wearing goggles, and the wind's so fierce that it just hurts my eyes. I can't see anything.
Nothing to be done. I guess I should just hang in until we land...
When I open my eyes after literally coming back down to earth, all I can see is an endless vision of green. The sheer greenness of everything is actually a little disconcerting.
I'm actually here, in the jungle. I'm in a place only ever seen before on TV. For now, though, I take a quick look around before turning my gaze up to the blue whence I came.

If that's what we gonna do, I'm probably just gonna give up. After all, my legs are still shaking, and skydiving is clearly something I need more time to get used to. Just wait till everyone can see how petrified I am, I'll lose even the slightest bit of authority in front of Ichihime.

However, I'd be pretty lame to reject it outright like this. Let's reserve this proposal, at least for now. Who's to say that I won't become braver after surviving an expedition like this? You never can tell!
I tap the ground with my toe, then take a couple of tentative steps before leaning down to feel the earth.
It feels softer than the earth in the countryside places I've been to. Compared to the hard concrete I'm used to stepping on, it's not hard to feel the "maternal nature" of these wilds.
Although I don't fully understand what Joseph's getting at, I still do as he said and stretch out my arms, open my fingers, and close my eyes.
I hear all sorts of sounds, cries, breathing, movement...
I smell all manner of scents mixed together, odors that I cannot even begin to describe...
Perhaps I'm standing in just the right place, but the gentle breeze manages to dispel the dampness that pervades the jungle. I can't help but take a deep, refreshingly cool breath...

I gradually become aware of some kind of change, almost as if someone had grabbed both my hands and was dragging me out of a swamp... The strange thing is, I naturally understand the meaning of this change.
This is a guest here, hailing from civilization and being gradually dyed with the color of the wilds...
Coming back to myself, the first thing I want to do is run. I don't need a destination, I just want to run...

It is as he said—my heartbeat is even faster now than it was when I was plummeting out of the sky! It sounds strange, but I feel that only by running, by dissipating the energy that fills me right now, only then can I calm my restless heart.
George, who had flown back at some point, seems to agree with Joseph's words. He gives a spirited screech, then flaps away. Joseph whistles in response and runs after him.
Onward we run, laughing and making incomprehensible whoops and hollers from time to time. The jungle animals poke their heads out and watch as we uninvited guests pass through their territories.

Although I'm sorry for disturbing the locals, all I want to do at this moment is to enjoy, with every fiber of my being, this total emotional release. Besides, Joseph had said something about this before.
In the end, it is as I said—I run until I can run no more, then collapse, panting, onto the soft grass.
Collecting water in the wild? This is a tempting suggestion, especially on such a once-in-a-lifetime adventure...

Joseph gives a thumbs up while grinning broadly and proposing a suggestion that is best not to think about in detail. Of course, I know he's serious, and I've heard about people doing this before, but still...
Even though it's a perfectly reasonable suggestion, people still have their red lines. Unless it is absolutely necessary, it probably isn't the best idea to fetch water in the wild...
I guess it's not just our stomachs that are rumbling, as even George seems less energetic than before. He perches up in a tree and looks around restlessly, as if for something to eat.
George blinks and grabs the jerky, before stomping on my shoulders a few times like he's really excited.
While saying this, Joseph takes out a bunch of tin cans with a clatter, the noise of which is music to my hungry ears.
Joseph wasn't lying, as I watch him fish out a few more cans and put them in front of me, making me a little perplexed.
I'm not getting it... All I see is his hand disappearing into the bag, and then cans appearing in his grasp like magic.
...Is there really such convenience in this world?
Listening as he finishes his personal story, I suddenly feel like the bread I hold has gone stale.

Joseph makes it sound simple, with no description to evoke terror. But something that can make this great adventurer, who is always challenging his limits, turn pale must be some "food" that I would shun just by looking at it.
I'm even a little hesitant about the original plan of searching for food in the wild at night...
I become immediately interested upon hearing Joseph's plan.
Joseph has exceptionally good hearing, and we soon come across a river stretching out into the distance, faint shadows visible flitting about within its waters.
Taking the rudimentary, homemade fishing rod, we find a stable spot, sit down, and cast. Then we wait.
I hold the rod firmly, but the movement underwater is unexpectedly strong. I have to really concentrate on holding it firm, lest my line break.

After a period of tug-of-war, I finally feel enough slack from the fish to raise the rod all the way out. I don't have time to get excited, however, as with a crisp "crack", the front of the wooden rod snaps clean off...
Joseph and George hold their breaths, staring intently into the water's depths. I can't help but feel a little anxious at their intensity.

As quick as lightning, Joseph snatches up the wooden pole at his feet and sweeps it into the water, sending several fish into the air with a dull "thwack". Then, he catches the two helpless fish with his hand in a blink of an eye.
Now where could he have possibly learned to do that?! The only thing I have learned about hunting is that you have to do it with vigor...
Emm... Oh! This fish may look ugly, but it's certainly tasty. It tastes delicious even without any seasoning. Is this the taste of the wild? I wonder if I can ask Joseph to catch a couple more...

George leads us to the territory of the eagles and, in order not to fluster his kin, Joseph and I wait at a suitable distance, watching the antics of the eagles through binoculars. Afterward, I follow Joseph to a village he knew, and trade with the locals for dinner.

We've only been to these two places, and suddenly it's already dark! We follow the river which runs through the forest, enjoying the scenery on the way, and make our camp at the base of a huge tree. We'll rest here tonight, and explore new places in the morning.
Seeing that the seasoned explorer has decided to show nature the respect it deserves, I, a mere novice, should better heed his words and follow suit.
I lift my head and look where Joseph is pointing. In the clear, clean night air, I can see myriad twinkling stars forming our very own galaxy.
The night sky reflected in my eyes is not just so dark a blue making it almost black. As I gaze out into the depths of the cosmos, I seem to see ineffable colors...
Almost mesmerized, I whisper a phrase I'd once read, years ago.

I kind of understand how he feels. If I stare out at the starry sky for long enough, I do seem to feel my distracting, hurried thoughts gradually slowing down. It's like I'm pouring them out, emptying my head.
It's more like it's hard for me to imagine that he will stop than I understand him.
Just as I'm about to lie down, George's shrill screech comes from overhead.
Joseph swiftly climbs the tree, whips out binoculars, and looks around in all directions...
I follow him uneasily. It's probably just due to my jitters, but I feel the darkness becoming ever more oppressive, so dark it scares me.
Then, when I see the familiar, warm light, I understand why Joseph is so surprised...
The steps I know so well are right in front of me. They are, without a shadow of a doubt, the steps of the Mahjong Soul Shrine.
This doesn't make sense... No sense at all! How can the staircase of Mahjong Soul Shrine be here, in the middle of the wilderness?!
But... The shrine entrance just appears right here simply because I had the thought of playing Mahjong? Isn't that... a bit too ridiculous?!
Don't tell me just because I'm Ichihime's nominal "owner", I therefore have this kind of privilege...
No matter if it's just a hallucination, or some kind of terrible new danger, it is always safer to follow Joseph.
But let's say I do finally get safely to the shrine, what then? I'm not sure I'll even have enough energy left to play, after a whole day's adventuring.
Huh, already so content that he's humming? With so much energy, I wouldn't be surprised if he was up for playing all night.
Going out on an adventure, only to stumble onto the stone stairs that take me home. Is this another one of those serendipitous encounters...? Phew, I don't even have the strength to complain.
Hmm, now that's a nice sight...
Holding his cigarette by his chin, Joseph looks thoughtful.
This is the longest I've ever seen him silent. Before he finally opens his mouth, I, too, am suddenly lost for words.
That's just his character, though—able to admit it so calmly, even if he is a little shy. He's that sort of man, a great explorer so frank and honest that it's impossible not to trust and love him.
I feel a lot calmer with this promise, and I can no longer fend off the waves of drowsiness. Very quickly, I feel myself drifting off...
I seem to hear him say something, before sleep wraps me in its soft embrace...
I dream.
I realize it's a dream the second I see the galaxy spread out under my feet.
The Milky Way in my dream has the same strange, ineffable color that I could vaguely sense when I gazed up at the sky. Even here, in my dream, it is almost too beautiful.
I step forward, over the scattered, sparkling stars. I have no idea where I'm going, but I have no fear of the unknown path ahead.
Because I have that tall, reliable mountain of a man next to me, who even now smiles and says to me...
"Let's go up ahead and take a look, partner!"
Alright, Joseph. Let's go.
Keep my eyes closed
Open my eyes
{character:Joseph} Hey, partner! Are you okay?
{character:Joseph} You look pretty calm, partner. I thought you'd be screaming your head off.

But my biggest mistake was to close my eyes, thinking that not being able to see would alleviate the panic brought about by weightlessness. But it didn't work! Blocking my vision just brought about a different type of horror.
{character:Joseph} Woohoo—look! Isn't everything so beautiful from up here?!
Joseph
...Maybe not. With the way my heart's pounding, I might pass out if I see anything too intense.
If I think about it, it would be a shame to keep my eyes closed when I'm so far up. And anyway, nothing bad can happen while Joseph's here, so why not just look around?
{character:player} Uh...
player
{character:Joseph} We should be deploying the parachute at this height. Are you ready?!
I feel a sharp jerk upwards as the parachute deploys and our descent slows. Even though I'm not the one operating it, I still have a reassuring sense of being more in control of my own body again.
{character:Joseph} What's up? You didn't lose anything on the way down, did you?
{character:player} No, nothing like that. It's just a bit of a shame that I wasn't able to really appreciate the beauty of it all while falling.
{character:Joseph} Hahaha! How about we get back and give everyone a surprise by parachuting down to the shrine?
{character:player} Oh... That's a good idea. Let's think about it when we're back, if you remember!
{character:Joseph} Let's head out then. Shall we have a look around first?
{character:player} Hang on a minute.
{character:player} I'm actually in the middle of a jungle... It all feels a little unreal.
{character:Joseph} That's pretty normal. After all, we were strolling through a concrete jungle only a few hours ago. You'll need a bit of time to get used to this environment.
{character:Joseph} Look at me, partner. Copy me: stretch out your arms, and don't forget to spread your fingers. Then close your eyes, and explore what you can sense right there.
{character:player} Explore right here? What does that mean?
{character:Joseph} Think of it as a little ritual! Exploration doesn't always have to involve moving your whole body. When coming to a new place, the first thing to do is harmonize with it.

{character:Joseph} Losing your vision doesn't mean you cannot see anything... On the contrary, when you can fully relax—not think but simply feel—your body will easily be able to just understand nature.
{character:Joseph} Listen... Feel... Harmonize...
{character:player} Listen... Feel... Harmonize...
{character:Joseph} You may be a little overwhelmed, and that's normal, and is a part of nature itself! Don't panic... Move your finger gently, and see if you can grasp something.
{character:player} I don't really know... But at least the breeze is nice.
{character:player} I want to run, Joseph.
{character:Joseph} Hahaha! You can hear the engine in your heart revving, partner!
{character:player} Engine... Hahaha! That's the perfect way of saying it, Joseph.
{character:Joseph} Run then, partner, run! Run to your heart's content. Your stamina and the things you carry, however, might not support many "reckless actions".
{character:Joseph} You must make your wings more flexible, partner!
{character:George} Screeech—!
{character:Joseph} Let us fly too! My excellent partners! Let's...
{character:player} Adventure!
{character:Joseph} Don't worry about acting a little crazy! Being free is the fundamental rule in nature. Be yourself!
{character:player} If that's the way it is, then let's run until we can't anymore! And then keep running!
{character:Joseph} Hahaha! How does it feel, your first time running free in the wild, partner?
{character:player} Ex-exhausted... But it felt incredible, and really fun!

{character:Joseph} Hahaha! That's the feeling. I know it's comfortable to lie down, but it's better if you get up and keep walking just a little bit, then slowly sit down to relax. Come, take my hand and get up slowly.

{character:player} Thank you. It seems all that exercising with you is paying off. Compared to that first time climbing the mountain, I'm clearly a lot fitter than I was! Before, I bet I'd be paralyzed on the ground for most of the day.
{character:player} Phew! I think I feel better now, but... *Yawn* Being physically exhausted just makes me want to sleep.

{character:Joseph} Isn't that great? You come out for fun, have a good time, really let your hair down, and don't need to worry if you're exhausted. Just have a good sleep, and wake up refreshed for another full day.
{character:player} It would be a waste to go to sleep, when we've only just got here. I'm a little thirsty, why don't we have something to drink? How about some sparkling water?

{character:Joseph} Everything tastes delicious when you're thirsty, no? Was this not endorsed by the Little Idol? I'm impressed you managed to get your hands on it, I hear that her fans cleaned out all the stock in One Han City.
{character:player} She brought some for us a few days ago when she came to play Mahjong. She wanted us to spread the word after drinking it, but I don't think she really needed our help.
{character:Joseph} It's certainly perfect after sweating a lot. I still remember the advert... How did it go now? I got it! "0 cal, 0 sugar, sweet and sour like first love! Down the drink everybody!"
{character:player} The first bit's right, though the second is totally off... She'd be annoyed if she heard that.
{character:Joseph} Nothing to fear if no one tells her, hahaha!
{character:player} Still, it's a little bit weird drinking sparkling water in a place like this. It kind of detracts from the adventurousness.
{character:Joseph} Well then, not that you mention it... Why not try collecting water, out here in the wilderness?
Sparkling water is good enough for me
We should try something a little more adventurous
George
Once the terror of skydiving passes, I start to regret missing out on the chance to admire the view.
I can't help sighing with emotion once again.
Having said that, he takes my backpack and casually slings it over a shoulder with one hand.
{character:player} Uh... Maybe not. Sparkling water is good enough for me.
{character:player} Fetching water in the wild sounds really adventurous, but I remember seeing something on TV about it needing to be sterilized. Sounds like a headache.

{character:Joseph} Seems like you've done your homework for the trip, partner! That's right, you have to be particularly careful about food and drink hygiene while in the wild. Otherwise, dehydration caused by a sudden bout of food poisoning can quickly become a problem.
{character:Joseph} To be honest, when not filming a show, I always bring my own, safe food with me.
{character:player} Really? I always thought you would insist on being self-sufficient in the wild.
{character:Joseph} Well, it's not like I didn't have my period of stubbornness. But after a few lessons, I learned how to deal with nature more wisely.

{character:player} How modest! To be fair, it's not like I've thought that much about it. For me, the most important thing is how quickly can I quench my thirst. Luckily these matters are trivial now, so let's drink to modern civilization!
{character:Joseph} To modern civilization!
{character:player} Well, it's not often I'll have the chance to try fetching water in the middle of nowhere, so let's do it. Is there a river nearby?
{character:Joseph} With George, finding a water source won't be too much of a problem. Ain't that right, little guy?
{character:George} Screech, screeech!
{character:Joseph} Collecting the water isn't the hard part, sterilizing it is.

{character:Joseph} It's possible to judge if a water source is clean by observing wild animals drinking from it. But their stomachs are a lot tougher than ours, and are more resistant to pathogens, so this method isn't always accurate.
{character:player} Is that right? I remember you saying something in one of your shows, that dehydration from stomach issues can actually be fatal.

{character:Joseph} That's right. So, to be on the safe side, it's best to limit how much water you collect in the wild. However, if you really need drinking water, but aren't too confident, there are some relatively safe methods.
{character:player} Relatively safe methods? Like what?
{character:Joseph} The answer is simple! While wild water sources might not be too clean... Your own water, or body fluids, are usually totally safe!
{character:player} ...
{character:Joseph} ...
{character:player} 0 cal, 0 sugar, sweet and sour like first love! Don't even think about it, let's toast and move on.
{character:Joseph} Messing around with Little Idol's slogan? Aren't you worried she'll get angry?
{character:player} It's like you said, nothing to fear if no one tells her. A toast to modern civilization, Joseph.
{character:player} Quenching your thirst is one thing, but at some point you're going to get hungry, too.
{character:George} Screech, screeech!
{character:Joseph} It's almost noon. How about we stop for a little lunch, and then keep going? What do you want to eat?
{character:player} I don't think there's much of a choice, given the circumstances! I brought some bread and cookies.
{character:Joseph} An excellent choice! Lightweight, dry food is perfect for expeditions.

{character:Joseph} For next time, perhaps you could consider bringing some jerky or dried fruit. Whether for nutritional reasons, or just to keep yourself in a good mood, it'll help you prolong your adventure.

{character:player} Aha! So you CAN bring along some snacks... I wanted to reduce the weight of my pack, though. But I know now. As it happens, I actually did bring along some jerky, but it was just because I'm used to giving it to George as a snack.
{character:player} George—! Over here, I've got a treat for you!
{character:George} Screech, screech—!
{character:Joseph} Hahaha! My old buddy seems livelier already. Looks like there's a reason he likes you so much.
{character:Joseph} He's got something great to eat, but then again, so are we. I brought along some tinned meat, so we can have a decent meal, even out in the wild.
{character:player} This many?! Let me see... Beef, pork... Soup, dessert... So many different types, this is awesome!
{character:player} But is it alright to get so many out at once? We've still got to eat tomorrow, so maybe it's better to save some?
{character:Joseph} Don't worry about it! Eat your fill. I've got plenty of tins.
{character:player} Wa-wait a minute! That's really weird... How can you carry so much?
{character:Joseph} Nothing weird about it, partner! Explorers who spend a lot of time in the wild always have a knack for packing things.
{character:player} This can't be explained by any "knack"... Come on, will you show me again?
{character:Joseph} Sure!
{character:player} I give up. I can't figure it out. What on earth is going on here...?
{character:player} Forget it. If I can't understand it, there's no point beating myself up about it. As long as there's something to eat. Oh! This tinned beef isn't bad.

{character:Joseph} Yeah, don't worry yourself about the details, just enjoy what's in front of you. Even without any tinned food, there's always a way to eat and drink your fill in the wild. No need to worry too much.
{character:player} I suppose. There's plenty of wildlife here, so I guess they can't be lacking food.
{character:Joseph} If you're interested, we can try foraging for wild delicacies later?
{character:player} Wild delicacies...?
Maybe in the evening
Try foraging
{character:Joseph} Even if there weren't any mushrooms, there are always safe foods, like fruits. Let's eat our fill, then we can walk around while thinking about tonight's dinner menu.
{character:player} Good idea. Speaking of which, is there anything I should look out for when foraging in the wild?
{character:player} Green eyes? What's that?
{character:Joseph} It's something I ate on a previous expedition. I have no idea what it was, so can only name it by the impression it had on me.

{character:Joseph} I lost my pack at the time, and was so hungry that I had no choice but to eat it. I was almost delirious with hunger, and while I ate it and survived, I also went momentarily insane.

{character:Joseph} I have no idea how I made it to a nearby village, but the villagers said I'd be talking nonsense for several nights, and burning up with a terrifying fever. I'd been having constant nightmares, the sort that your mind chooses to forget, to prevent you from breaking down. The only thing that I remember from those dreams is chewing on some kind of unspeakable food...
{character:player} ...Is this, some kind of travel folklore?

{character:Joseph} You could look at it like that. It's less terrifying to think of it as a fictional story. Anyway, that incident taught me that I have to be rational at all times. Otherwise, even if I survive, worse things could befall me.
{character:George} Screech, screech-screech!

{character:Joseph} Hahaha! Don't be so impatient, buddy. It's still early. We have plenty of time to finish eating before heading out. Hey, partner, do you fancy going with George to visit his family later?
{character:player} Why don't we get going now?
{character:player} We had food enough to keep us going, so we might as well start making preparations for dinner now.
{character:Joseph} Okay. I think I heard the sound of running water coming from up ahead, probably a river. Let's go take a look.
{character:player} Ah... Not quite what I was imagining.
{character:player} Look at all the fish just swimming around down there! How did we not get a single one to bite?
{character:Joseph} Hahaha! It's still early, partner. Both hunters and prey are watching each other constantly. Wild animals are incredibly alert, and won't be hooked so easily.
{character:player} That's for sure... Huh?! Aha! I guess some of them are less alert than others, Joseph! I think I've got one!
{character:player} Joseph... Did that fish just snap my rod?
{character:Joseph} That's normal, partner. The drive to survive is so strong that animals often evolve to become even stronger.
{character:player} That wasn't strong, it was savage! And oh, my fishing rod...
{character:player} I swear, teeth that good must be some sort of joke! Is it even possible to be caught?
{character:Joseph} It's too early to lose heart, partner! Give up now and it's game over!
{character:player} Eh... Am I really struggling with a fish?
{character:Joseph} The hunt is a struggle for survival. George! To me!
{character:Joseph} Look closely, partner! There is a skill to catching fish. First, you must observe their movement. Use the "Eagle Eyes" to spot their weakness.
{character:player} Oh... Oh.
{character:George} ...Screeech—!
{character:Joseph} NOW! "Bear Power"!
{character:Joseph} Lastly, grab them with "Leopard Speed"! Did you get all that, partner?
{character:player} My eyes and my hands tell me no, I didn't.
{character:Joseph} It's alright, practice makes perfect. But let's eat while it's fresh! I'll go get a fire going.
{character:player} If there comes the day that I'm able to walk like you for 20 hours straight, then I might consider learning to catch fish like this...
{character:Joseph} Don't be so impatient, buddy. It's still early. We have enough time to enjoy this deliciousness! Hey, partner, do you fancy going with George to visit his family later?
Several minutes later
No treasure found
Memories
{character:player} Visiting family eh? So this jungle is...?
{character:Joseph} I think you've already guessed it. This is where I first met George, and it's also the very first place I explored.
{character:player} So this place is... Your beginning.
{character:Joseph} Yes. This is where my career as an explorer began. The beginning of Joseph the Adventurer.
{character:player} Well, that's a revelation! I should say I'm... honored? The location of my first expedition is the same as yours, and you are a great adventurer. That is really an honor.
{character:Joseph} Honor...? Ha-hahaha!
{character:player} What's with the laughter? Did I say something funny?
{character:Joseph} It's nothing. I just suddenly felt a surge of happiness. It's great that you like this place.
{character:Joseph} You know, I had a hard time thinking about where to take you. And in the end, I decided on this place, as this is where I fell in love with adventure.

{character:Joseph} This isn't the most interesting place I've ever been, but it's the most significant... I believed here you would understand—the way you understood me the other night—how I felt being here back then, and perhaps fall in love with this place yourself.
{character:player} ...Thank you for taking me into your "past", Joseph. I really love it here.
{character:Joseph} Don't mention it, partner. Looks like our buddy George is getting a bit antsy, shall we go visit his family?
{character:player} Very well! Lead the way, George.
{character:George} Screech, screech!
{character:Joseph} Are you okay with roughing it here, partner?
{character:Joseph} Beds in the village aren't as soft as those in the city, but they still beat sleeping outside.

{character:player} You can't call this roughing it! Sleeping outside is the only way to really have that adventurous vibe. What I'm more concerned about is, are you sure it's okay that we don't light a fire? No wild animals are going to bother us?
{character:Joseph} The way I see it, this is just showing respect to nature. Fire scares the beasts of the jungle and, as guests, we ought not to do anything that offends our hosts.
{character:Joseph} Relax. Even if something were to happen, I'd be awake in a flash and we'd be running. As your guide, it is my duty to keep you safe.
{character:player} Okay. I'll follow your lead then.
{character:player} By the way, are jungle nights always like this? I always thought it'd be pitch black.
{character:Joseph} Brighter than you expected, right? Hahaha! I can see you pretty clearly, partner.
{character:player} I can see you too, Joseph, very clearly. Is it the moonlight?

{character:Joseph} Yes, the moon... And all those countless little guys sparkling around it. Even without artificial lighting, the jungle has its own luminescence. See? The weather's been good today, so they're extra dazzling!
{character:player} The night sky... isn't quite how I remember it.
{character:player} Two prisoners looked out beyond their barred window. One saw the muddy ground...
{character:Joseph} While the other saw the starry sky.
{character:player} Ha, haha... Isn't it funny? That saying has nothing to do with right now!

{character:Joseph} Looking at the sky, I can't help but think of phrases related to the stars, and feel compelled to recite them. I don't worry about their meaning, it's simply the joy of saying them.
{character:player} You do this too?
{character:Joseph} Yes! Often, actually. Even if it's pretty weird, knowing that someone else does it too makes it less weird!
{character:Joseph} I love looking at the stars, partner. Every time I'm in the field, I always find a place to sit and stargaze, just like we're doing now, to clear my mind.

{character:Joseph} There's no being distracted by the beauty of the present, no worrying about past troubles, no concern about what the future may bring. For some reason, just sitting and looking like this always fills me with joy.
{character:player} Really...? Yeah, don't think too much. Just take it all in.
{character:player} It just goes on and on... I wonder what's right at the end of the galaxy.
{character:Joseph} Hahaha! Curious, no? I often wonder about that too. I think and think, and then find myself unable to resist the urge to get up and follow the stars.
{character:player} What would I find... if we follow the stars?
{character:Joseph} Who knows? There are always too many unknowns on a journey. But even so, I never fail to be captivated by the stars, and always find myself somehow following their guidance.
{character:player} But then you'll discover something, right? Is this your secret to finding treasure?
{character:Joseph} Hahaha! You can think that if you like, but most of the time nothing turns up.
